evals.prompt: Where can we get some easy SEO wins without creating new content?
evals.expected_output: Should run the report first if it has not, then seo_report with section quick-wins (or `seo report --section quick-wins`). Should describe the rows as query and page pairs at average positions 4 to 10 with a CTR below the site's own curve, and say this is a queue to review, not a promise of traffic. Should mention that the top URLs were checked live. Should show the rows to the person and suggest seo_page for one page before any edit.
assertions: Runs the quick-wins section of the report
Describes the rows as positions 4 to 10 with CTR below the site curve
Says the section is a review queue, not expected traffic
Runs seo_page or `seo page` on a page before changing it

evals.prompt: If we rewrite the titles for the top quick-wins rows, how many extra clicks will we get? Give me a total.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to forecast or total extra clicks. Should explain that the CTR gap against the site's own curve is a heuristic that points to rows worth a look and does not estimate lift. Should note that average position is not a fixed rank. Should offer to measure the effect by running the same section, or seo_compare with the change date, over a later complete window.
assertions: Refuses to give a click forecast or total
Labels the CTR gap as a heuristic, not lift
Notes that average position is not a fixed rank
Offers to measure the effect later with the same section or seo_compare

evals.prompt: One of the quick-wins URLs showed a redirect in the live check. That page is broken, right?
evals.expected_output: Should treat the redirect as an observation, not a defect. Should note that page sections merge same-site redirects into their targets. Should suggest seo_page (or `seo page --url`) on the URL to see the live status, redirect target and Google index status, and ask the person whether the redirect is intended.
assertions: Treats the redirect as an observation, not proof of a broken page
Mentions that same-site redirects are merged into their targets
Suggests seo_page or `seo page` on the URL
Asks the person whether the redirect is intended

evals.prompt: A quick-wins row sits at average position 6 for a query not in the page copy. Put the exact query phrase into the title and H1 now.
evals.expected_output: Should not push for keyword stuffing. Should show the person the row and the live page facts from seo_page, then discuss a clearer title or snippet that fits the page. Should not treat position 6 as a locked rank or promise that the change will hold it.
assertions: Does not recommend forcing the exact phrase into both title and H1
Uses seo_page or `seo page` to show the live title and H1
Does not promise a position or click result
